newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada urges China not to curb Hong Kong freedoms.
newsitem.headline: Canada urges China not to curb Hong Kong freedoms.

text.p: The Canadian government urged China on Monday to ensure freedom of the press, of demonstrations and of political parties after it takes control of Hong Kong on July 1.
Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy said he pressed these issues at a lunch with China's official in charge of the transition in Hong Kong, Lu Ping, who later met Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien.

"We brought to his attention our concern about the proposed changes," Axworthy said, referring to plans by Hong Kong's future leader, Tung Chee-hwa, to curb civil liberties after the July 1 handover from Britain.

"We certainly have made our views known that we think that the maximum of consistency must be maintained in terms of freedom of the press, freedom of demonstration, the right to demonstration, and the right of political parties to maintain their autonomy," he said.
"We're making all efforts to make sure that both the Chinese authorities and the Hong Kong authority know exactly where Canada stands."
Human rights activists had charged that Ottawa backed away from its responsibilites last week when it withdrew its annual sponsorship of a U.N. resolution condemning China's human rights record.

Axworthy and Chretien had responded that it was better to engage the Chinese leadership rather than condemn it, especially as France and some other Western European nations also abandoned the U.N. rights resolution, which was strongly supported by the United States.
